beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Keys restore a church. More keys turn it into a kingdom death cannot break up. This episode is about the visitors who brought the rest.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: April sixth, eighteen thirty. In a Fayette, New York farmhouse, the church the devil had taken off the earth stood on it again — same name, same offices, same authority as Galilee.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Six years later, the young church finished its first temple at Kirtland, Ohio — built at crushing sacrifice. The women crushed their own china into the plaster so the walls would catch the light. They wanted a house fit for visitors.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: They got them. April third, eighteen thirty-six — Easter week. After the sacrament, Joseph and Oliver bowed behind the pulpit veils in solemn prayer... and the veil of the visions opened. First came the Lord himself:

beats.speaker: jesus
beats.text: For behold, I have accepted this house, and my name shall be here; and I will manifest myself to my people in mercy in this house.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: His eyes were as a flame of fire; the hair of his head was white like the pure snow; his countenance shone above the brightness of the sun; and his voice was as the sound of the rushing of great waters, even the voice of Jehovah.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Then, one by one, the last holders brought the keys home. Moses — the same Moses — committed the keys of the gathering of Israel.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Then Elias, restoring Abraham's covenant — the promise that every family on earth could be blessed, folded whole into the church again.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And last, the visitor Malachi had promised in the closing words of the Old Testament — the last prophecy most Bibles print:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: and he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Elijah — the Carmel prophet, the fire-caller — stood in the Kirtland temple and handed over the sealing power: authority to bind on earth and have it bound in heaven. Families welded past the grave. The dead — reachable.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Feel what that last one means. The devil's version of death rips every family apart forever — every till-death-do-you-part is his fine print. Elijah's keys tear the fine print up. And look around: the whole world caught family-history fever within a few generations of that afternoon. The pull is real.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: So: the church came back on April sixth. But after April third, eighteen thirty-six, it was more than a church — a kingdom with gathering orders, Abraham's covenant, and death-proof glue. The devil spent seventeen centuries taking things off the earth. Heaven put every one of them back in six years.

card.speaker: narrator
card.text: Till death do you part was the devil's fine print. Elijah tore it up.
